A. CRITICAL ISSUES & RECOMMENDED SOLUTIONS — MSI (NEC)
Five critical delivery gaps converted into accountable, time-bound corrective interventions.
ISSUEACTIONOUTCOME
Critical issue
Recommended Solution
Non-adherence to project implementation, O&M and software activities
Approved plans for project implementation, O&M and software activities were not adhered to.
Submit a duly signed plan for all three activities
Plan duly signed and approved by higher management. (Submitted)
Resource constraints
Shortage of qualified manpower, inexperienced field staff and no full-time Project Manager.
Immediate Deployment of qualified core team
Deploy approved PM, architects, specialists, engineers and district teams with a backup pool.
Application instability
ANPR/FRS failures, SSO issues, software instability and storage faults.
Stabilize priority applications
Run a dated defect-removal plan with OEM L3 support, regression testing and release sign-off.
Operations readiness gap
Required operators are not deployed at PS C2i and designated locations.
Deploy and certify operators
Implement shift rosters, role-based training, SOP walkthroughs and operational acceptance.
SLA restoration breaches
Camera restoration exceeds two days and complaint resolution remains delayed.
Activate 24x7 SLA control desk
Automate ticket ageing, escalation alerts, restoration ownership and recurring breach review.
Accelerated closure pathway
1
0-7 daysResources and defect baseline
2
8-30 daysStabilize apps and deploy operators
3
31-60 daysIntegrations, SOPs and SLA automation
4
Closure gateJoint UAT and formal acceptance
Target impactStable applications, staffed operations, faster restoration and measurable contractual compliance.

B. CRITICAL ISSUES & RECOMMENDED SOLUTIONS — ISP (RAILTEL)
Five network and service-management gaps translated into resilience and monitoring interventions.
ISSUEACTIONOUTCOME
Critical issue
Recommended Solution
Non-adherence to project implementation and O&M activities
Approved plans for project implementation and O&M activities were not adhered to.
Submit a duly signed plan for all three activities
Plan duly signed and approved by higher management. (Submitted)
Single sub-vendor dependency
One fiber subcontractor across 16 districts creates capacity and continuity risk.
De-risk the vendor model
Add qualified fiber partners and RailTel-controlled district teams with crews, spares and vehicles.
Frequent fiber cuts
Limited maintenance manpower and extensive overhead fiber cause recurring outages.
Build route resilience
Audit hotspots, protect feasible overhead stretches, add redundancy and pre-position repair kits.
Repeated link downtime
Multiple sites experience downtime below contracted availability and uptime standards.
Strengthen 24×7 Network Operations
Automate incidents, escalation, MTTR tracking, RCA and corrective action for repeat breaches.
Centralized NMS absent
The mandated centralized monitoring platform remains undeployed, limiting visibility.
Commission centralized NMS
Enable real-time status, alarms, bandwidth visibility, ticket integration and role dashboards.
Accelerated closure pathway
1
0-7 daysLinks, crews, spares and hotspots
2
8-30 daysNOC, interim monitoring and alternate crews
3
31-60 daysNMS and route protection
4
Closure gateResilience test and SLA acceptance
Target impactResilient connectivity, real-time visibility, reduced downtime and auditable SLA performance.
